hint.acid_type: Binary acids do not contain oxygen (HX, H₂X). Oxyacids contain oxygen (e.g. HNO₃, H₂SO₄).
hint.dissoc_acid: Acids dissociate by releasing H⁺ ions.
hint.dissoc_base: Bases dissociate by releasing OH⁻ ions.
hint.dissoc_salt: Salts are products of acid-base reactions — they dissociate into metal cations and acid-residue anions.
hint.pH_scale_acid: pH %s is less than 7 — acidic reaction.
hint.pH_scale_basic: pH %s is greater than 7 — basic reaction.
hint.oxide_types: Basic oxides = metal oxides; acidic oxides = nonmetal oxides. Amphoteric oxides react with both acids and bases.
hint.base_solubility: Soluble bases (strong): NaOH, KOH, LiOH, Ca(OH)₂, Ba(OH)₂. Others are sparingly soluble.
hint.hc_alkane: Alkanes — CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Only single C−C bonds.
hint.hc_alkene: Alkenes — CₙH₂ₙ. Contain one C=C double bond.
hint.hc_alkyne: Alkynes — CₙH₂ₙ₋₂. Contain one C≡C triple bond.
hint.org_carboxylic: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group -COOH.
hint.org_ester: Esters are formed from the reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol.
hint.elem_period: %s is in period %s of the periodic table.
hint.read_from_card: Read the atomic mass from the element card
hint.count_row: Count the row from the top of the table — that is the period number
item.oxide.basic: basic: metal oxide → reacts with acids (→ salt + H₂O)
item.oxide.acidic: acidic: nonmetal oxide → reacts with bases and H₂O (→ acid)
item.oxide.amphoteric: amphoteric: reacts with both acids and bases (ZnO, Al₂O₃)
item.oxide.neutral: neutral: does not react with acids or bases (CO, NO)
step.count_period: Count the row from the top of the table — that is the period number
